steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' to use React components and state management.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React and the useState hook into your TypeScript file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports for building React components with state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state management in TypeScript.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX. Use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint:
Define a component called App that returns a JSX element, like a
or

. Remember to use TypeScript syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named App is defined and returns JSX.
successCriteria: The App component is defined with the correct name and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named App and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is not defined correctly. Ensure it's named App and returns JSX.

steps.title: Define union type for shapes
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a union type called Shape that can be either the string literal 'circle' or 'square'.
steps.hint: Use the pipe symbol | to create a union type. For example: type Status = 'active' | 'inactive';
steps.analogousExample:
// Defining a union type for status
type Status = 'active' | 'inactive' | 'pending';
steps.expectedOutcome: A Shape type is defined using union syntax with 'circle' and 'square' as possible values.
successCriteria: The Shape type is defined as a union of 'circle' and 'square' string literals.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a union type for shapes. This allows TypeScript to know that Shape can only be either 'circle' or 'square'.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure Shape is defined as a union type with both 'circle' and 'square' using the pipe | operator.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Define a type called Shape that can be either 'circle' or 'square' using union syntax (type Shape = 'circle' | 'square';).

steps.title: Define intersection type for detailed shape
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a new type called DetailedShape that creates an intersection type combining the Shape union type with an object type containing radius: number and sideLength: number properties.
steps.hint: Use the & operator to create an intersection type. The new type should include all properties from Shape plus the two additional number properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a DetailedShape type that combines the Shape union with additional properties, demonstrating how intersection types work in TypeScript.
successCriteria: The DetailedShape type is defined using the & operator, includes the Shape union type, and adds radius: number and sideLength: number properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an intersection type that combines multiple type definitions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure DetailedShape uses the & operator and includes both the Shape type and the object with radius and sideLength properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to use the & operator to intersect Shape with { radius: number, sideLength: number }.

steps.title: Initialize state with union type
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, initialize a state variable named 'shape' using the useState hook. The state should be typed with the Shape union type and have a default value of 'circle'.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with a type annotation to specify that the state variable can only hold values from the Shape union type.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state with a union type
const [status, setStatus] = useState<'idle' | 'loading' | 'error'>('idle');
steps.expectedOutcome: A state variable 'shape' is declared with the Shape type and initialized to 'circle'.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with the Shape type annotation and 'circle' as the initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state with a union type, ensuring 'shape' can only be one of the allowed values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to type the state variable with the Shape union type and set the default to 'circle'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state variable 'shape' was not properly initialized with the Shape type and default value 'circle'.

steps.title: Create a type guard function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'isCircle' that takes a parameter of type 'Shape' and returns a boolean type predicate indicating if the shape is a circle.
steps.hint: Use a function declaration or arrow function with a return type annotation. The function should check if the parameter equals 'circle'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function 'isCircle' is defined with proper TypeScript type predicate syntax.
successCriteria: Function 'isCircle' is defined, takes a 'Shape' parameter, returns a boolean type predicate 'shape is "circle"', and correctly checks equality.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a type guard function. This will allow TypeScript to narrow the union type at runtime.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function has the correct parameter type, return type predicate, and returns the proper boolean check.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check the parameter type, return type annotation, and the equality check inside the function.

steps.title: Create handler to toggle shape
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named toggleShape that switches the shape state between 'circle' and 'square' values.
steps.hint: The toggleShape function should update the state using setShape. You can check the current shape value and set the opposite one.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleShape function is defined that will switch the shape state between 'circle' and 'square' when called.
successCriteria: The toggleShape function is defined inside the App component and updates the shape state appropriately.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a toggleShape function that will switch between 'circle' and 'square' values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly toggles between 'circle' and 'square' values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleShape function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that switches between 'circle' and 'square' values.

steps.title: Create function using intersection type
steps.instruction: Define a function named calculateArea that accepts a parameter of type DetailedShape and returns a number representing the area.
steps.hint: Inside your component, create a function that takes a DetailedShape parameter and returns a number. You can use the shape property to determine which area formula to apply.
steps.expectedOutcome: A calculateArea function that accepts DetailedShape and returns a number will be added to your component.
successCriteria: The calculateArea function is defined with a DetailedShape parameter and returns a number type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a function that uses the intersection type as a parameter.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it accepts DetailedShape as a parameter and returns a number type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateArea function is not properly defined. It should accept DetailedShape and return a number.

steps.title: Add basic component structure
steps.instruction: Return a div container with the class name 'shape-app' from your App component.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div element that has the specified class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns a div element with the class 'shape-app'.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element with className='shape-app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the basic container for your shape application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div element with exactly the class name 'shape-app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element with className='shape-app'. Check your syntax.

steps.title: Display current shape with type guard
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a paragraph that displays the current shape value and uses the type guard function to show a shape-specific message.
steps.hint: Use the shape state variable and call the type guard function to conditionally render different text based on the shape type.
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element that shows the current shape and a message based on whether it's a circle or not.
successCriteria: The paragraph displays the shape state value and uses the type guard function to conditionally show shape-specific text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the current shape and used the type guard to show a shape-specific message.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it uses the type guard function to conditionally display different messages for circle vs other shapes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph doesn't properly display the shape value or use the type guard function. Check that you're calling the type guard and rendering conditionally based on its result.

steps.title: Add toggle button and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the div that calls toggleShape when clicked and displays 'Toggle Shape' as its text.
steps.hint: Use the onClick prop on a button element to call the toggleShape function you defined earlier.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with an event handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the UI that, when clicked, will toggle between shape values using the toggleShape handler.
successCriteria: The button element is present with onClick={toggleShape} and displays 'Toggle Shape' text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that will trigger the shape toggle functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but it's missing either the onClick handler or the correct text. Make sure it calls toggleShape and says 'Toggle Shape'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or incorrect. Add a <button> with onClick={toggleShape} and text 'Toggle Shape'.

steps.title: Demonstrate intersection type usage
steps.instruction: Inside the component, create a DetailedShape object and call calculateArea with it, then display the result in a paragraph below the existing content.
steps.hint: Define a constant variable with the DetailedShape type, then call your calculateArea function with that object, and render the result in JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now demonstrate intersection types by creating a DetailedShape object, calculating its area, and displaying the result in the UI.
successCriteria: A DetailedShape object is created and passed to calculateArea, and the result is displayed in a paragraph element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully demonstrated intersection type usage by creating a DetailedShape object and displaying its calculated area.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but ensure you create a DetailedShape object, call calculateArea with it, and display the result in a paragraph.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a DetailedShape object, calling calculateArea with it, and displaying the result. Review intersection types and function calls.
